articles.title: Oil settles up on renewed US-Iran hostilities and threat of Red Sea closure
articles.content: Oil prices climbed significantly on Friday, reaching their highest point in over a month. Escalating hostilities between the United States and Iran intensified attacks across the Gulf region. Shipping routes face potential closure, impacting global oil flows and prices. Saudi Arabia has redirected significant crude exports to avoid the Strait of Hormuz. Ukraine also reported striking a Russian oil refinery in its conflict.

articles.title: Gold set for biggest weekly drop since early June on inflation, rate-hike worries
articles.content: Gold prices saw an increase on Friday, driven by escalating U.S.-Iran tensions. These geopolitical events fueled energy prices and inflation concerns, impacting market sentiment. Higher inflation fears reinforced expectations of potential U.S. interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve. While gold is a hedge against inflation, higher rates typically pressure the non-yielding metal. Other precious metals like silver, platinum, and palladium also experienced weekly losses.

articles.title: Tech selloff weighs on European shares ahead of ECB meeting next week
articles.content: European stocks edged lower Friday, influenced by a global tech sell-off and Middle East tensions. Tech stocks experienced a significant decline this week, impacting major AI beneficiaries. Utilities and defense sectors saw gains, while luxury brands faced headwinds from reduced tourist spending.

articles.title: JSW Steel’s Q1 profit soars 2x YoY on robust topline growth
articles.content: JSW Steel's profit more than doubled year-on-year to 4,696 crore in the June quarter. Robust revenue growth and higher volumes aided the company's strong financial performance. Consolidated revenue from operations rose around ten percent on year to 47,364 crore. Total expenses grew less than four percent on year, which helped profitability. The company's net debt also saw a significant reduction during the period.

articles.title: Wall Street's chip index enters bear market! Is the AI bubble finally going bust?

A new AI model from China's Moonshot and concerns over heavy AI spending triggered a broad selloff across global technology stocks.

articles.title: Fairfax picks up half of 3-year government bonds at auction
articles.content: Fairfax Financial Holdings likely purchased government bonds as a prelude to acquiring IDBI Bank.  This marks the company's second significant bond purchase in recent months.  The Canadian firm is reportedly preparing to invest capital for a potential IDBI Bank stake.  Fairfax aims to secure a major stake in the government-owned lender.  The IDBI Bank privatisation process has been ongoing since October 2022.

articles.title: Reliance Retail's Q1 profit drops 14% YoY but revenue rises 8%
articles.content: Reliance Retail Ventures reported a fourteen percent profit decline last quarter. Revenue from operations grew eight point two percent year-on-year. Reliance Retail expanded its store network to over twenty thousand locations.

articles.title: Netflix shares tumble over 10% as slowing growth, less viewership data spook investors
articles.content: Netflix recently saw a significant drop in its share prices following a forecast that indicated slower revenue growth. Additionally, the streaming service announced it would cut back on reporting viewership statistics, which has raised investor anxiety regarding its future trajectory. Analysts attributed this downturn to a lackluster lineup of content released this year, leading to a considerable drop from its stock peak.

articles.title: US Fed official warns of 'broad-based' inflation as firms urge action
articles.content: A top Federal Reserve official said Friday that stubbornly high inflation is her bigger concern right now, warning that firms are urging the US central bank to act against rising prices. "Persistently high inflation is the bigger concern," she said.

articles.title: Chipmakers and other high-flying stocks slide as AI trade wobbles
articles.content: As July commenced, global tech stocks faced a notable decline, predominantly driven by chip shares. This drop indicates investor profit-taking alongside worries regarding the sustainability of AI expenditures. The Philadelphia Semis Index is close to entering bear market territory after facing a steep decline. Additionally, the Chinese AI model Kimi K3 has heightened scrutiny of US tech investment returns, while the market eagerly anticipates earnings reports from Alphabet and Tesla.
